From: Elena Voronin <evoronin@heliosdx.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA addendum + order form language for enterprise engagement

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the per-route observability. Before we move to procurement, our legal and platform teams need a custom SLA addendum to sit alongside the MSA/SOW and the Order Form. High level ask: we need explicit commitments for regional availability and latency for our production traffic.

Key asks:
- 99.95% regional availability (US-east primary) on a monthly rolling basis;
- P95 inference latency target <= 120ms for 1-2k concurrent connections per region;
- Credits capped at 3 months of monthly recurring charges;
- Clear failover / regional fallback behavior and notification windows;
- Telemetry checklist: token-level latency, per-route error rates, and breach evidence (logs/traces) retained for 12 months.

Please let me know what you can commit to and whether you can provide a redline for the Order Form that captures the uptime/latency thresholds and the remedy schedule. If possible, we need this completed and routed to procurement by EOD Tuesday (16 Apr).

I've cc'd contracts@heliosdx.com for procurement coordination.

Regards,
Elena Voronin
Head of Infrastructure
HeliosDX

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the timeline. We're aligned and I'll coordinate internally to get a first-pass addendum and order-form language to you by COB Monday (15 Apr). A few quick clarifying questions so the draft matches your needs:

1) Data residency: do you require persistent data to stay in us-east only, or is regional processing with cross-region replication acceptable?
2) Is the 12-month evidence retention a hard requirement or a preferred target? We typically offer 12 months for audit logs but can confirm for traces/metrics.

I've attached an initial working draft (HeliosDX_SLA_Draft_2029-04-14.docx) and the proposed Order Form language (OrderForm_HeliosDX_2029-04-14.pdf) — these are drafts; legal will redline.

Thanks — will follow up Monday with the redlined package.

On Mon, Apr 15, 2029 at 11:02 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached an initial working draft ...

Team — read through Sofia's draft this morning. High-level legal comments and proposed redlines in attached PDF (legal_redlines_2029-04-14.pdf). Summary:

- Availability target: 99.95% monthly is acceptable as a contractual commitment, but we should:
  * Narrow the definition of "regional availability" to the specific clusters that will serve HeliosDX (avoid open-ended language that covers all future regions).
  * Add an exclusion carve-out for scheduled maintenance windows (with advance notice and maximum maintenance percentage per quarter).

- Latency: including a P95 threshold in the SLO is OK, but avoid hard monetary credits tied solely to P95; recommend linking latency credits to both sustained P95 breach (>= 3 partial days in a 30-day window) and concurrent capacity constraints.

- Remedies cap: 3x monthly charges is higher than standard; propose 2x MRC cap and an exception approval path for extraordinary failures.

- Evidence & retention: confirm that telemetry used as "evidence" will be a snapshot export (JSON/log bundles) with signed chain of custody for audit — need Ops to confirm retention windows for traces (Marcus).

- Operational requirement: define the notification cadence (initial incident notice within 15 minutes, root cause update within 24 hours for Sev1) and attach the runbook reference.

Please incorporate the suggested edits into the next draft. Aditya — please advise if the proposed remedies cap (2x) is acceptable commercially for DEAL-4821. Marcus — need your confirmation on telemetry retention and the 15-minute notification.

-Kim

Attachment: legal_redlines_2029-04-14.pdf (redline + risk memo)

Subject: Proposed SLA addendum and Order Form language (updated) — HeliosDX

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached are the updated artifacts: a clean addendum with our proposed edits and the Order Form language updated to call out the regional availability clusters and the remedy schedule. Highlights:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly for defined us-east clusters (definition section 1.2). Scheduled maintenance excluded (48-hour rolling notice, maintenance limited to 0.5% of calendar month).
- Latency: P95 <= 120ms target; credits only trigger on a sustained P95 breach (>= 3 distinct days in 30-day window) or when correlated with capacity shortages.
- Remedies: cap set at 2x monthly recurring charges; we include an approval path for higher claims with executive review.
- Evidence: We'll provide export bundles (logs/traces/metrics) for the 12-month retention window; Marcus confirmed feasibility for metrics and traces subject to data retention settings in the Order Form.
- Notifications: initial incident alert within 15 minutes for Sev1, RCA updates within 24 hours; runbook reference included.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached final draft (HeliosDX_SLA_Draft_2029-04-14.docx) and the Order Form PDF.
2) If acceptable, sign via the DocuSign link below so we can attach the addendum to the MSA and complete procurement.

DocuSign prepare link: https://www.docusign.net/prepare/HELIOSDX-SLA-4821 (placeholder — will push final envelope once you confirm)

If you need any small edits, we can accept a single round of partner redlines and then go to signature. Please let me know if procurement needs any additional evidence items for their audit.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Enterprise Programs
Redwood Inference
